title: Check yourself: what BiFunction and computeIfAbsent do not give you

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Per this page, what happens to `repeat.compose(upper)` when `repeat` is a `BiFunction<String, Integer, String>`?

options.text: It does not compile, as that interface lacks such a method
options.says: The page says BiFunction has no compose() and marks the call as a compile error.

options.text: It runs upper first, then passes that result as both inputs
options.says: The page says the method does not exist on BiFunction, so nothing runs.

options.text: It runs upper last, on the string that repeat has produced
options.says: That is what andThen does; the page says the other method does not exist on BiFunction.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

questions.stem: Per this page, in which map is a single `computeIfAbsent` call atomic?

options.text: In a plain HashMap, though not in a ConcurrentHashMap
options.says: The page says that in a plain HashMap it is simply one call instead of three, not an atomic one.

options.text: In a ConcurrentHashMap, though not in a plain HashMap
options.says: The page says it is atomic in ConcurrentHashMap, and merely shorter in a plain HashMap.

options.text: In both of them, since the check and the put share one call
options.says: The page separates the two: atomic in ConcurrentHashMap, merely shorter in a plain HashMap.

concepts: computeIfAbsent is atomic in a ConcurrentHashMap but is only a shorter call in a plain HashMap.
BiFunction has andThen but no compose.
